title.narrative: Reduce the average malaria prevalence in children aged less than 5 years from 7% in 2017 to less than 3.5% in 2025. Achieve Universal Health Coverage and reaching targets for health related Sustainable Development Goals by 2030 - Tanzania (United Republic) (01-Jan-2024-31-Dec-2026)

description.narrative: Tanzania (United Republic), Malaria, Ministry of Finance of the United Republic of Tanzania (MoF)This program has the following goals: The national goal is to reduce the average malaria prevalence in children aged less than 5 years (pfpr6-59 months) from 7% in 2017 to less than 3.5% in 2025. To reduce malaria transmission from the Annual Parasite Incidence (API) of an average of 121 per 1000 in 2019, to less than 30 per 1000 in 2025. To achieve Universal Health Coverage and reaching targets for health related Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. The objectives of this program are: Reduce malaria parasites transmission from 2.9 in 2020 to 0.1 in 2025 by maintaining recommended evidence-based vector control interventions according to the targeted malaria risk strata. To prevent the occurrence of mortality related to malaria infection from 4 per 100,000 Malaria Mortality rate in health facilities in 2020 to 1 per 100,000 in 2025 through universal access to appropriate diagnosis and treatment and targeted provision of preventive therapies for vulnerable groups. Increase the proportion of councils with very low malaria transmission risk from 20% in 2020 to 35% in 2025 through provision of timely and reliable information on malaria and its control needed to take appropriate actions in different transmission risk and ensure resources are used in the most cost-effective manner. Ensure 100% of malaria commodities are received as per supply plan by maintaining timely availability of safe and quality malaria commodities and supplies at the delivery points.. To strengthen an enabling environment where individuals at risk from malaria are empowered to protect themselves and their families from malaria and seek proper and timely malaria-treatment. Increase proportion of malaria control inteventions implemented annually from 63% in 2020 to 90% in 2025 by strengthening efficiency and effective coordination of malaria implementation strategies via accountable partnership.. Expand access to a package of high-quality, safe, and acceptable integrated, people centered health services; service delivery management and quality improvement systems. Accelerate shift from disease-specific to integrated and interoperable supply chain systems. Accelerate the development and use of integrated digital data platforms. Strengthen community systems that support integrated community responses. Accelerate shift to support more integrated, national laboratory systems
